findings.text: Early GART IOMMU bring-up is gated on northbridge GART capability, global disable controls, aperture availability and an AGP information source. When memory extends beyond the low 32 bit range but the path is unavailable it warns about software mapping fallback and returns without enabling hardware translation.

Successful bring-up ensures aperture mapping, establishes translation sizing and allocation state, carves the IOMMU window from the top of the aperture, removes that window from the direct map with cache maintenance before enabling hardware, then switches DMA handling to GART with its shutdown hook while disabling software IO translation.

The device visible window lacks full CPU cache coherence, so the design removes it from the direct map and performs full cache writeback before enabling translation. Unmapped entries use a shared zeroed scratch page so speculative peer reads do not abort.

Option parsing accepts a leading numeric translation size plus textual controls for full flushing behavior, AGP use, aperture repair, forced or allowed aperture use, and a memory aperture fallback with optional order value.

Northbridge discovery uses a PCI vendor device table for misc functions across K8 through later families with an empty terminator, a small bus device range table with terminator, and a global info object holding a count plus array pointer plus feature flags alongside a separate cached flush word array.

Northbridge caching is idempotent once a nonzero count exists. It sizes by node count, requires a misc handle per node and otherwise releases everything and reports absence, optionally records a link handle, then records GART and L3 capability flags according to family model and stepping.

Node function lookup validates the node index against the architectural maximum and returns the PCI handle for the requested function on the node base slot plus node offset, or null when out of range.
Early northbridge identification requires an AMD class vendor, excludes Zen class parts, then matches the device portion of the supplied identifier against the misc table.

MMCONFIG range query fails with null unless vendor and minimum family match, the configuration base control reads successfully and its enable bit is set. On success it fills a memory resource with base and span derived from base and bus range fields.
Subcache query returns zero without partitioning support and otherwise returns a four bit field selected by core identifier from a link configuration word.

Subcache update rejects missing partitioning support or masks wider than four bits, snapshots reset and BAN state once, adjusts BAN mode around partial disable, programs a per core shifted mask with sibling controls in high positions, then restores BAN if the link word returned to reset.
GART flush word caching does nothing without the GART feature. Allocation failure clears that feature and reports disabled support, while success snapshots one configuration word per node.

Erratum 688 handling applies only to family 14H with initialized northbridges and a present link device whose inspected configuration bit is clear. When applicable it runs a per CPU control update on all processors and reports the workaround.
Northbridge subsystem initialization succeeds immediately on non AMD class vendors. Otherwise it caches northbridges, caches GART state and applies the family 14H erratum workaround.
Instruction cache configuration control number is hex C0011021; the workaround sets bits 3 and 14.
One mutex serializes all management network and HSMP index data pair accesses through PCI configuration space.
Management network index is at configuration offset hex 60 with data at hex 64; HSMP index is at hex C4 with data at hex C8.

Low level management access rejects out of range nodes, uninitialized root table and missing per node root, then under lock programs the address port and either writes or reads the data port, converting firmware status to errno and warning on address programming failure.

Public read uses the standard index data pair and treats an all ones result as missing device, clearing the output. Public write and HSMP read write forward node address value and direction to the common helper.

Debug interface exposes node, address and value controls. Node selection parses an integer and rejects indices beyond node count; address selection parses an integer unconditionally; value read performs a management read of the stored pair and value write marks the kernel out of spec before performing the management write.
Root enumeration walks host bridge class devices, keeps only function zero devices from AMD class vendors, and returns the next match.

Management initialization runs only on Zen class parts and is idempotent once roots exist. It reserves whole configuration space for every enumerated root, allocates a per node root table, derives roots per node with a hypervisor aware fallback, assigns one root per node skipping extras, and optionally creates debug files when enabled by boot option.
Initialization reserves entire configuration space per root so user space cannot race index data sequences; without successful reservation the common accessor refuses all operations.
Fallback aperture allocation is constrained between 512 megabytes minimum and 4 gigabytes maximum, naturally aligned to its size.

Aperture tracking records a start frame and length from base and order, reports frames inside that interval as not RAM for crash and memory views, and registers view callbacks when configured. One build variant makes exclusion a no operation.

Fallback allocation caps order to keep size at or below one gigabyte, derives size from a 32 megabyte base shifted by order, allocates an aligned range inside the allowed window, marks it not saved across suspend, and returns zero on failure.

Capability search requires the capability list status bit, starts from the capability pointer, iterates a bounded number of entries while the pointer stays in the extended range, masks low bits, stops on invalid identifier and returns the matching offset or zero.

AGP aperture sizing reads the size register, normalizes unusual encodings, derives an order from population count with a floor for small sizes, reads the base from configuration words masked to aperture granularity, falls back to the prior northbridge order when the computed window would exceed 4 gigabytes, and validates placement before returning the base.

Bridge search scans buses slots and functions with early exit on absent device and on non multifunction headers, selects host class bridges carrying an AGP capability, and returns the first decoded aperture while recording that a valid bridge was seen.
Boot defaults enable aperture fixing and E820 correction, set fallback order to one representing 64 megabytes without forcing, and leave the translation aperture disabled until allowed.
Logging prefixes use the module name for northbridge code and an AGP label for aperture code.
